_: The ONE case list every href guard is held to. A URL a person reads out of an email, a Feed row, or an ATS board, about to become a live `href`. Four call sites render these: webapp/lib/url/safe-href.ts (the landing page and the two pipeline/queue cell renderers import it), webapp/lib/capture/schema.ts:safeUrl (after its www. repair), and core/digest_links.py:safe_href (the email). The TS and Python guards are held EQUAL against this file by webapp/tests/unit/safe-href.test.ts and tests/core/test_safe_href_parity.py, because a guard the store trusts and a guard the renderer trusts that disagree by one backslash is exactly the C2 review's M6. The algorithm is pure string work on purpose: new URL() and urlsplit disagree on %40 and on an empty authority, so neither parser is the authority — the authority is this list.
reject_reason_note: expected "" means the guard blanks it; a string means the guard returns it unchanged (trimmed). No guard ever REPAIRS here — the www. repair is capture-only and happens before the guard sees the value.

THE M6 BUG: a browser normalises backslash to /, so this reads as good.com and resolves to evil.com. Rejected by the backslash rule before any parse.
any backslash anywhere is refused; the two parsers disagree on what it means
%40 is an encoded @, i.e. userinfo in disguise. Node's URL throws on it and Python's urlsplit keeps it as the host, so the parsers disagree — the authority-has-% rule makes both refuse.
empty authority. new URL() reads host 'nohost'; urlsplit reads none. The empty-authority rule makes both refuse the malformed thing.
